newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard aims for cut in jobless by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard aims for cut in jobless by 1999.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday he aimed for a reduced unemployment rate by 1999.
"I knew when I became prime minister that I couldn't get rid of unemployment in the space of a year, I can't," Howard told Sydney radio 2UE.
"And I'm not saying to the people now that I can get rid of it over the next two years," he said.
"I'll be disappointed if I haven't brought it down a bit by the time of the next election."
The conservative Liberal-National government has repeatedly said it had no intention of setting an unemployment rate target.
Howard said in March he had no reason to back away from his 1991 statement that unemployment was unlikely to fall below five percent in his lifetime.
Australia's unemployment rate was at 8.7 percent in March, down from 8.8 percent in the previous month and has shown no trend decline at all since late 1995.
The government is forecasting an 8.5 percent unemployment rate by the June quarter.
